svg.title: Build a Measurable Commercial Service in Thirty Days
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-08-thirty-day-commercial-launch; chart type: timeline_roadmap; title: Build a Measurable Commercial Service in Thirty Days; subtitle: Four weekly milestones establish scope, infrastructure, pilot evidence, and a delivery-ready operating review.; chapter number: 12; epistemic tag: operating_framework; assumptions note: Numeric values are elapsed-day endpoints: 7, 14, 21, and 30. This sprint builds operating capability; the canonical first-deal window remains one to four months. Pilot activity uses authorized resources and eligible contacts, with spend bounded by the selected $5,000–$40,000 startup cash plan.; caption: Finish day thirty with documented evidence and a clear continue, repair, or stop decision for each pilot cohort. Do not manufacture accepted leads, booked revenue, or a signed client to satisfy the calendar.; stages: label: Days 1-7; value: Choose one niche and write the acceptance contract.; numeric value: 7.0; detail: Select territory and buyer profile; interview prospective clients; define accepted-appointment criteria, duplicate rules, fees, and dispute handling. Produce a channel requirements checklist and a cash forecast through the four-month first-deal window.; label: Days 8-14; value: Configure systems and test every suppression and routing path.; numeric value: 14.0; detail: Authenticate authorized domains, configure CRM fields and least-privilege access, and connect scheduling and call routing. Use synthetic test records to verify opt-outs, duplicate handling, assignment failures, and evidence retention.; label: Days 15-21; value: Run a bounded pilot and inspect qualification evidence.; numeric value: 21.0; detail: Activate a small eligible account cohort with explicit spend and contact limits. Review delivered accounts, positive replies, held appointments, rejection causes, and contractor time daily; repair failures before increasing volume.; label: Days 22-30; value: Review unit economics and prepare accountable client delivery.; numeric value: 30.0; detail: Reconcile cohort counts, accepted units, invoices when earned, and actual costs. Demonstrate the reporting pack, assign each exception owner, and pursue a retainer under the written scope without treating pipeline value as revenue.

text.title: Build a Measurable Commercial Service in Thirty Days
text.tspan: Build a Measurable Commercial Service in Thirty Days

circle.title: label: Days 1-7; value: Choose one niche and write the acceptance contract.; numeric value: 7.0; detail: Select territory and buyer profile; interview prospective clients; define accepted-appointment criteria, duplicate rules, fees, and dispute handling. Produce a channel requirements checklist and a cash forecast through the four-month first-deal window.

text.title: Choose one niche and write the acceptance contract.

circle.title: label: Days 8-14; value: Configure systems and test every suppression and routing path.; numeric value: 14.0; detail: Authenticate authorized domains, configure CRM fields and least-privilege access, and connect scheduling and call routing. Use synthetic test records to verify opt-outs, duplicate handling, assignment failures, and evidence retention.

text.title: Configure systems and test every suppression and routing path.

circle.title: label: Days 15-21; value: Run a bounded pilot and inspect qualification evidence.; numeric value: 21.0; detail: Activate a small eligible account cohort with explicit spend and contact limits. Review delivered accounts, positive replies, held appointments, rejection causes, and contractor time daily; repair failures before increasing volume.

text.title: Run a bounded pilot and inspect qualification evidence.

circle.title: label: Days 22-30; value: Review unit economics and prepare accountable client delivery.; numeric value: 30.0; detail: Reconcile cohort counts, accepted units, invoices when earned, and actual costs. Demonstrate the reporting pack, assign each exception owner, and pursue a retainer under the written scope without treating pipeline value as revenue.

text.title: Review unit economics and prepare accountable client delivery.

Assumptions: Numeric values are elapsed-day endpoints: 7, 14, 21, and 30. This sprint builds operating capability; the canonical first-deal window remains one to four months. Pilot activity uses authorized resources and eligible contacts, with spend bounded by the selected $5,000–$40,000 startup cash plan.
